title: Mikel Arteta says he needs to understand ‘exceptional’ Arsenal teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly
content:
Mikel Arteta says “understanding” Myles Lewis-Skelly better was key to his decision to start the 19-year-old in midfield in Arsenal’s crucial wins over Fulham and Atletico Madrid.

Lewis-Skelly, who became an England international in his breakthrough season last year, has started just 16 of the 32 matches he has appeared in this season.

The teenager started 15 Premier League matches in the 2024-25 campaign, but his start against Fulham last weekend was just his third in the league this term, and his first-ever senior start in midfield – the position he came through Arsenal’s academy playing.

Asked on the timing of the decision to use Lewis-Skelly in midfield, Arteta told reporters on May 8: “It’s been a process of understanding him better. Him understanding a lot of the standards that are required when you play or don’t play that much at this level. To understand the reason why you play or not as well.

“He’s been exceptional. His attitude, the way he’s been training, the way he’s been supporting the boys when he hasn’t played. He’s given us every sign to think that when we give him the chance, he’s going to respond in the manner that he’s done.

“But he has done it, and it’s not easy – especially when you have not played that much – to look that fresh, confident, energetic and playing with that determination. It’s something that is surprising.”

Part of the reason for Lewis-Skelly breaking through last season were the fitness issues of left-back Riccardo Calafiori. The Italy international started 16 of Arsenal’s first 17 league games this season, however, and was replaced by summer signing Piero Hincapie.

Lewis-Skelly has been unlucky not to start in midfield in some instances this year, initially named in that position for Arsenal’s FA Cup tie with Wigan Athletic on February 15 before an untimely Calafiori injury in the warm-up forced him to return to left-back.

Arteta has admitted that he did not plan all along to use Lewis-Skelly as a midfielder at this stage of the season, feeling that “intuition” has been vital in recent weeks.

This has been the case with Eberechi Eze playing off the left wing with Martin Odegaard in central midfield recently too, who the Arsenal manager has also spoken about needing to “understand” better.

Asked what he grew to understand more about Lewis-Skelly, he added: “I need to put on the Myles Lewis-Skelly hat to understand how he’s feeling.

“He’s a boy who was playing with the Under-18s, Under-21s, sometimes he wasn’t even playing. He comes through in a position he’s never played before, he’s exceptional and everyone’s talking about him. He goes to the national team, comes back from pre-season and starts to realise that maybe he’s not going to be a starter.

“So you need to go through those emotions, not only you but the people next to you as well. You have to navigate through that, and that’s not easy. I understand that. It’s easy when it’s going so well for you, but when it goes the other way, the temptation is going to be to start pointing at people.

“I need to understand that. I need to guide him and I need to give him my perspective on the reasons why he wasn’t playing so much. He took it on board, not the first time, but after three or four times I think he realised if it’s not this way I don’t think it’s going to happen.”

There is no guarantee that Lewis-Skelly will continue as Arsenal’s starting central midfielder alongside Declan Rice for the rest of the season, but his performances against Fulham and Atletico have helped give Arsenal the momentum and balance they were lacking last month.

He has looked fresher than Martin Zubimendi, who is Arsenal’s second-most used outfield player in all competitions this season (4,132 minutes), while Calafiori has allowed their left flank to be more expressive and free-flowing.

With five days between Arsenal’s Champions League semi-final win over Atletico and their Premier League trip to West Ham, it would not be a major surprise if Arteta started Calafiori at left-back again.

On the other side, Arteta will have to decide between Ben White and Cristhian Mosquera again, as he confirmed that starting right-back Jurrien Timber will miss Sunday’s game against West Ham United on Sunday.

Asked whether the Netherlands international’s groin issue is more complicated than it first seemed, the Arsenal manager said: “Yes, and that’s been probably the most difficult thing to manage, with the player, with myself as well, because we didn’t expect it to take so long, and at the moment he’s not fit to play.”

Arsenal could take another big step toward becoming Premier League champions at the London Stadium on Sunday, May 10, but Manchester City have the opportunity to close the gap to two points first as they host Brentford on Saturday, May 9.
